item.title: Linear Response for Self-Consistent Transfer Operators on Graphons
item.description: arXiv:2611.10167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop the response theory of the equilibrium state of a large heterogeneous network of weakly coupled uniformly expanding circle maps. The thermodynamic limit of such a network is governed by a Self-Consistent Transfer Operator (STO) acting on measures fibred over a graphon $W$, as introduced in \cite{MPT2025}. We prove that in the weak coupling regime the unique attracting fixed point $\phi^\star(\alpha)$ of the STO depends on the coupling strength in a Lipschitz, and then differentiable, way in a scale of fibrewise Sobolev spaces, and we derive a linear response formula. Our main result is that at zero coupling the response factorises: its derivative along the fibre $z$ equals $\barW(z)\,\Up$, where $\barW$ is the degree function of the graphon and $\Up=-(\Id-P)^{-1}[P(H_\rho\rho)]'$ is a universal profile depending only on the local dynamics and on the coupling function. To first order the heterogeneity of the statistical response across the network is therefore dictated by the degree profile alone, and the finer topology is invisible; the susceptibility of a node is proportional to its degree, so hubs respond most. The topology enters at higher order through a tree expansion: the perturbative coefficients of the equilibrium, defined unconditionally by an explicit recursion, are combinations --- with universal coefficient functions --- of the rooted homomorphism densities of trees with $m$ edges. We prove that the first two coefficients are the genuine asymptotic ones, the second producing the mean degree of the neighbours of $z$. We also obtain a response formula for perturbations of the graphon itself, Green--Kubo expressions for observables, and the prediction that in a finite network the linear susceptibility of a node is proportional to its normalised degree.
item.dc:creator: Herbert M. C. Maquera

item.title: Up or down by half: a family of Collatz-type maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.10311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Each Collatz step changes a positive integer by roughly half: odd inputs go up and even inputs go down. We vary the directions while keeping the step size. Write x=2^m k (k odd), and let S be a set of positive integers. Define T_S(x)=(3x+1)/2 if m=0, 3x/2 if m is in S, and k otherwise. The map T_S^- differs only at odd x, which it sends to (x+1)/2. The usual Collatz map is T_emptyset. Assuming the independence of 2-adic valuations along odd-to-odd steps yields random-walk models with drifts (1+rho(S))log_2(3)-2 for T_S and rho(S)log_2(3)-2 for T_S^-, where rho(S) is an explicit series. Every T_S^- is contracting; T_S is contracting exactly when rho(S)<log_3(4/3), approximately 0.2619. We prove density results, classify interval sets S, and give a criterion ensuring every T_S^- orbit reaches 1 or (2,3). For seven contracting maps T_S, three with rho(S)=1/4 just below the threshold, computations show that every n<2^34 (n<1.668*10^10 for S={1}) reaches one of at most five cycles; stopping-time statistics match the model to 3-5 digits. We study branching maps, where any member of a family may be applied at each step. Boundedness of a family implies boundedness of each member; in particular, boundedness of {T_emptyset,T_{3}} would imply that no Collatz orbit diverges. For {T_emptyset,T_{1}}, a rule depending only on x mod 32 has positive drift (10/17)log_2(9/8) for almost every 2-adic starting point. Thus almost all n have reachable sets containing values larger than n^1.05; residues modulo 2^L, L<=10, cannot prove unboundedness. Finally, we define unified maps in which valuations also determine the direction at odd inputs. The cases x=1 mod 4 govern their behavior: if they go down, every block is dominated by the corresponding Collatz map (and a census finds only the cycles (1), (2, 3) and (3, 5) with smallest element below 10^9); if they go up, the maps behave like T_S.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Vasilyev

item.title: Quenched large deviation estimates for skew product systems with the almost-sure fiber specification property
item.description: arXiv:2611.10350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish quenched level-2 large deviation estimates for empirical measures of measurable skew products with compact metric fibers over an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation on a Polish space. Our hypotheses are formulated through lower and upper energy functions, which describe the exponential decay of conditional measures of fiber Bowen balls. Under almost-sure fiber specification, we prove lower bounds for open sets. Upper bounds for closed convex sets require only the upper energy condition, and upper semicontinuity of fiber entropy removes the convexity restriction. When these hypotheses hold with a common energy function \(T\), we obtain a quenched level-2 large deviation principle with a good rate function \(I_T(\rho)=\int T\,d\rho-h_\rho(F)\) on invariant measures with the prescribed base marginal, and \(+\infty\) otherwise. We also derive quenched level-1 large deviation principles for bounded continuous observables and a quenched Laplace principle. As an application, we consider skew products that are Anosov and topologically mixing on fibers. For Gibbs equilibrium states associated with random potentials $f$ having integrable two-sided Bowen variation, we construct bounded strictly positive common energy functions by coboundary corrections. This construction identifies the large deviation rate on invariant measures as \(\pi_F(f)-h_\rho(F)-\int f\,d\rho\), where \(\pi_F(f)\) denotes the fiber topological pressure.
item.dc:creator: Xue Liu, Xiaomin Zhou, Xiaoyao Zhou

item.title: Directional Ergodic Theorems, Ergodicity, and Weak mixing for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.10409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study Birkhoff and von Neumann type ergodic theorems for $\mathbb Z^2$-measure preserving systems along irrational directions. This leads us to a further investigation of directional ergodicity and weak mixing. Additionally, we show that our framework (dynamical definitions) is equivalent to the spectral definitions of directional ergodicity and weak mixing introduced by Robinson, Rosenblatt and \c{S}ahin \cite{RRS2023} for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions. We note that in their recent paper \cite{RS2026}, Robinson and \c{S}ahin established the equivalence between dynamical and spectral directional weak mixing for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions using an approach fundamentally different from the one employed in the present paper.
item.dc:creator: Chunlin Liu, Kairan Liu, Tao Yu

item.title: An introduction to discrete dynamics in condensed sets: orbits, periodic loci, and arithmetic examples
item.description: arXiv:2611.10438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate discrete dynamics internally in the topos Cond of condensed sets. For an endomorphism $f\colon X\to X$, we construct orbit quotients, backward histories, preimage trees, and periodic loci as objects evaluated on profinite parameter spaces. The framework recovers global-section dynamics, fully faithfully embeds compact Hausdorff systems, characterizes the invertible extension, and is compatible with inverse limits. It organizes $p$-adic congruence towers and shows, for a Cantor-type non-Archimedean Julia set, that classical periodic points can be dense although the internal periodic locus is not isomorphic to the compact condensed Julia set.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Memorias de la Sociedad Matem\'atica Mexicana 10 (2026) 87-122
item.dc:creator: J. Rogelio P\'erez-Buend\'ia

item.title: Directional weak mixing and directional Kronecker for $\Z^2$-actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.10761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $T$ be a measure preserving $\Z^2$-action on a Lebesgue probability space $(X,\mu)$ and let $L\subseteq\R^2$ be a $1$-dimensional subspace. For a rational subspace $L$, direction $L$ weak mixing corresponds to weak mixing for the measure preserving transformation $T^{\vv_0}$, where $\vv_0$ is a primitive vector in $\Z^2$ generating $L$. For an irrational direction $L$, we study two different definitions of direction $L$ weak mixing, and show that they are the same: ``Dynamical'' direction $L$ weak mixing is defined to be the absence of any direction $L$ Kronecker factors. These factors are defined in terms of almost periodicity along a finite width direction $L$ strip in $\Z^2$. ``Spectral'' direction $L$ weak mixing is defined as the absence of any direction $L^\perp$ line segments $I\subseteq\T^2$ with positive spectral measure. We also give a spectral characterization of the directional Kronecker property defined in \cite{liuxu}, and provide examples of $\Z^2$-actions $K$ that are direction $L$ Kronecker.
item.dc:creator: E. Arthur Robinson, Jr., Ay\c{s}e A. \c{S}ahin

item.title: On the Bendixson criterion for attractors of dynamical systems in metric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.10918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the Bendixson criterion for attractors, originally proposed by R.A. Smith for the finite-dimensional case and subsequently extended by M.Y. Li and J.S. Muldowney to Banach spaces. First, we give a concise proof of the criterion for general dynamical systems (semiflows, mappings, cocycles) in metric spaces using \v{C}ech cohomology. This approach allows for a significant weakening of previously known conditions while simultaneously resolving existing misunderstandings. Second, for compact invariant sets of semiflows that are topologically one-dimensional and possess zero first cohomology (e.g., attracting a superset with zero first cohomology), we prove that any chain recurrent point within the invariant set must be an equilibrium. In the proof, we construct a global strict Lyapunov function using Whitney-Bebutov sections. Third, we generalize and refine R.A. Smith's theorem concerning the finiteness of the set of fixed points for analytic mappings, as well as M.L. Cartwright's theorems on to almost periodic flows.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Anikushin

item.title: Frequency shifts: non-soficity, absence of specification and intrinsic ergodicity
item.description: arXiv:2611.10995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $p_c\in(0,1)$, the frequency shift $\Sigma(p_c)\subset\{0,1\}^{\N}$, introduced by Becker and Baraviera, is the closure of the shift orbits of the set of sequences in which a symbol $1$ is followed by $1$ exactly when the density of ones up to that position does not exceed $p_c$. We show that $\Sigma(p_c)$ is never sofic and never has the (weak) specification property. For $p_c=\frac{k}{k+1}$, with $k\ge1$, we describe $\Sigma(p_c)$ completely: $\Sigma(\frac12)$ is the coded system generated by $\{0^m1^m\}_{m\ge1}$, while for $k\ge2$ the shift $\Sigma(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is not transitive, but every invariant probability measure is supported on the coded system generated by $\{0^m1^{km}\}_{m\ge1}$. For every $k \ge 1$, the topological entropy of $\Sigma(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is $\frac{\log2}{k+1}$, and, using the Climenhaga--Thompson criterion, we prove that $\Sigma(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is intrinsically ergodic.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Reyes

item.title: Forward and pullback attraction under worst-case and ergodic exponents in a predator-prey model with bounded random refuge
item.description: arXiv:2611.11026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a predator-prey system with logistic prey, Holling type II response and a prey refuge fluctuating randomly within a band, driven by a bounded transformation of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. Bounded noise yields a deterministic compact set attracting forward uniformly in the realisation, alongside the random pullback attractor, and we compare the two. The smallest such deterministic set, the minimal uniform attracting set, is the kernel of the control system in which the accessible fraction is any measurable band-valued function, and it meets the coexistence region exactly when the upper worst-case invasion exponent of the predator is positive, whereas the pullback attractor is governed by the ergodic invasion exponent, which decides the predator's fate pathwise. When the predator becomes extinct, the closure of the union of the fibres of the pullback attractor equals the minimal uniform attracting set if and only if the upper worst-case exponent is nonpositive, and otherwise the inclusion is strict and the latter is invariant under no realisation. When the predator persists, the essential closure of the union of the fibres contains, for every frozen environment in which the predator invades, the equilibrium or a periodic orbit of the frozen system, and every state the control system can reach from them. The predator is uniformly persistent when the lower worst-case exponent is positive and almost surely not when it is negative. The ergodic exponent lies below its deterministic counterpart by an amount comparable to the curvature of the response times the variance of the accessible fraction.
item.dc:creator: Ever F. Cruzado-Quispe, Javier L\'opez-de-la-Cruz, Paulo N. Seminario-Huertas

item.title: Proximal Myhill-type theorems for $m$-expansive amenable semigroup actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.11161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Garden of Eden theorem relates surjectivity to a weak injectivity condition for cellular automata on amenable groups. Li extended the Myhill implication to expansive actions of countable amenable groups with weak specification. We consider two simultaneous relaxations: the group is replaced by a cancellative amenable semigroup, and expansiveness by m-expansiveness. The loss of ordinary expansiveness removes homoclinic rigidity, so we introduce a proximal analogue of pre-injectivity. Our main result shows that, for a surjective action of an infinite countable cancellative left-amenable semigroup on a compact metric space, m-expansiveness plus weak specification forces every continuous equivariant map injective on each proximal set to be surjective. The proof uses entropy detection at a fixed scale, a strict entropy gap from weak specification, and finite multiplicity to produce proximal pairs from uniformly close points. We also give a one-dimensional variant under shadowing and examples clarifying the assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Boxu Huang

item.title: Local study of generic dynamical systems on the b-symplectic plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.11171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Gb$ be the group of germs of planar diffeomorphisms, fixing the origin, which preserve the standard b-symplectic form. The group acts on itself, under the usual left-right action and we identify, in the generic case, a simple representative of each orbit, depending on a non-vanishing, univariate, function. We then study the action of $\Gb$ on b-symplectic vector fields. For those fields that do not vanish at the origin, we establish a flow-box type theorem, while, for those that do vanish there, we show that the study of their conjugacy classes reduces to a classification of functions. We present this classification, when the origin is a regular point for these functions, while if it is a critical point, we present the orbits of their 2-jets. Finally, we address the problem of whether an element of $\Gb$ can be realised as the time-1 map of a b-symplectic vector field.
item.dc:creator: Stavros Anastassiou

item.title: Learning calibrated probabilistic forecasts using Koopman mode decomposition and the continuous ranked probability score
item.description: arXiv:2611.11257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Well-calibrated forecasting for non-linear dynamical systems is essential in science and engineering applications such as fluid dynamics and weather prediction. We present a forecasting method combining probabilistic machine learning with the structured linear dynamics of Koopman mode decomposition. Within this framework, the observation, linear dynamics, and state reconstruction operators are constructed using standard machine learning architectures, producing predictive distributions via the pushforward of injected noise samples. The model is trained using a proper scoring rule, the continuous ranked probability score, to directly target calibrated, accurate forecasts. The approach is validated on two non-linear ordinary differential equation examples and two partial differential equation examples, vortex shedding and cavity flow, using both large and small, noisy datasets. Results demonstrate that known Koopman eigenfunctions and spectra can be identified and used for accurate forecasting. The model can also produce multi-modal predictive distributions, demonstrated for a trajectory initialised on the boundary between two basins of attraction. Uncertainty is captured by the sample ensemble spread, with spread--skill ratios close to one over the training horizon in several experiments, although for extended rollouts and noisy datasets, the ensemble may become under- or over-dispersed. In low-noise experiments, temporal rollout is generally accurate for at least twice the training horizon, and up to twenty times in some cases. Approximation quality is comparable to a deep ensemble approximation over the training horizon, but at a reduced computational cost and with better robustness in identifying Koopman eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin M. Kent, Richard E. Turner

item.title: Onsager--Machlup Theory and Transition Pathways for Degenerate Stochastic Systems with Multiplicative Noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.11270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Noise-induced transitions between metastable states are central to many nonlinear stochastic dynamical systems, and most probable transition pathways provide an effective means of revealing the underlying transition mechanisms. In this work, we develop an Onsager--Machlup framework for degenerate stochastic dynamical systems driven by multiplicative Gaussian noise. We first derive the Onsager--Machlup action functional for the additive-noise case using the Girsanov transformation, and then extend the result to multiplicative noise through a Lamperti-type transformation. The resulting functional provides a variational characterization of the most probable transition pathway, from which we derive the associated Hamilton--Pontryagin boundary value problem. We further recast the variational problem as an equivalent optimal control problem and propose a neural-network-based numerical method for computing the most probable transition pathways. Numerical examples are presented to illustrate the theoretical framework and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed computational approach.
item.dc:creator: Weichen Wu, Ying Chao, Jinqiao Duan

item.title: Schmidt games for nonautonomous Liverani--Saussol--Vaienti maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.11758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Liverani--Saussol--Vaienti (LSV) maps form a family of piecewise differentiable dynamical systems on $[0,1]$ depending on a parameter $a>0$. These maps are expanding away from a neutral fixed point. In this paper, we study Schmidt games for nonautonomous compositions of LSV maps with arbitrary parameter sequences in a compact subinterval of $(0,\infty)$. For every countable set $P\subset[0,1]$, we prove that the set of points whose orbit closure is disjoint from $P$ is absolute winning on $[0,1]$. Our proof combines a potential game argument with an interval tree constructed from successive returns.
item.dc:creator: Haoyang Ji

item.title: Rigidity and existence of profiled expansive solutions of the $N$-body problem with homogeneous potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.11945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study expansive solutions of the $N$-body problem with homogeneous potentials of degree $-p$, where $p>0$. We establish asymptotic rigidity for arbitrary solutions with admissible profiles. For general admissible profiles and $0<p<2$, we obtain convergent power-log expansions whose exponents are governed by the leading profiles. In the hyperbolic case, we derive a more explicit analytic representation for all $p>0$, extending Chazy's Newtonian result. Together with the author's recent results [Wu, 2026], this yields a bijective parametrization of hyperbolic solutions near infinity by their asymptotic velocities and offsets. We also establish the existence of free-time minimizing solutions with arbitrary prescribed initial configurations and admissible asymptotic profiles for $0<p<2$, covering the hyperbolic, parabolic and hyperbolic-parabolic regimes. In the hyperbolic case, the result extends to all $p>0$, including possibly collisional initial configurations in the strong-force regime $p \ge 2$. Furthermore, we prove that when $p \neq 2$, every solution with an admissible asymptotic profile is eventually a free-time minimizer.
item.dc:creator: Yutong Wu

item.title: A Poisson-bracket operator for Hamiltonian separability: intrinsic geometry and exact defects
item.description: arXiv:2611.12015v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Additive separation of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation depends on the Hamiltonian and on the canonical variables, and this paper introduces a five-input Poisson-bracket operator whose values on canonical pairs reproduce the Levi-Civita separability expressions. On a symplectic product structure its off-diagonal values are intrinsic, since they equal a symplectic pairing of the sector Hamiltonian fields and measure the Frobenius obstruction of a Lagrangian distribution, and their vanishing yields a local separation theorem. Because the operator is cubic in the Hamiltonian, its perturbation expansion is exact and defines a linearised separability operator and a defect functional. For Hamiltonians with a cyclic angle, the linearised operator divided by the squared rotor frequency is an angle derivative of the Melnikov integrand, so that the defect integrated along a homoclinic orbit decides the first-order splitting of the separatrix. Closed-form defects are obtained for the polar-nodal normal forms of satellite theory and, through a covariance of the operator on level sets, for Kerr geodesics. Used for coordinate selection, the defect singles out the separating focal distance of the Euler two-centre problem as its unique nondegenerate minimum, and for axisymmetric potentials it shows that the prescriptions of Sanders and Vasiliev are two weightings of the same St\"ackel residual. The residual selector and Binney's shell-orbit fit improve both actions over the median prescription for 48 and 50 of 50 orbits in a flattened logarithmic potential, whereas the operator selector lowers the 90th-percentile action spread of 50 orbits in a Miyamoto-Nagai potential from 2.90% to 0.91%.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Martinusi

item.title: Functions with finite energy on the Sierpinski gasket
item.description: arXiv:2611.12174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a systematic framework for constructing finite-energy functions on the Sierpi\'nski gasket using Lipschitz maps and various classes of contractions. Several properties of the constructed functions are investigated, including the min--max property and bounds for their energy. Several examples of finite-energy functions, along with their graphical representations, are provided to illustrate the functions constructed using the proposed framework. It is further shown that finite energy does not necessarily imply membership in the domain of the Laplacian. The framework is then applied to a class of fractal interpolation functions on the Sierpi\'nski gasket, for which necessary and sufficient conditions for finite energy are established under suitable contractivity assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Harsha Gopalakrishnan, Srijanani Anurag Prasad

item.title: Rates in the weak invariance principle for slowly mixing sequential dynamical systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.12263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain rates of convergence in the weak invariance principle for certain classes of slowly mixing sequential dynamical systems. In particular, for systems satisfying a Functional Correlation Bound with rate $n^{-\gamma} \ (\gamma>1)$, we establish an explicit bound in the Wasserstein-$r$ metric for $1\le r<\gamma+1$ whenever the variance grows at a sufficiently fast polynomial rate. The proof is based on Bernstein's ``big block--small block" method. Examples covered by our result include sequential heterochaos baker maps and sequential LSV maps. In particular, for random LSV maps over an ergodic base, we obtain rates in the quenched weak invariance principle.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Fleming-V\'{a}zquez, Zhe Wang

item.title: Lower intermediate dimensions of classical Denjoy minimal sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.12323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the $\theta$-intermediate dimension of the minimal set of the classical $C^{1+\delta}$ Denjoy map, an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of the circle not conjugate to a rigid rotation. This follows on from work of Kra and Schmeling, who showed how the box and Hausdorff dimensions may differ, depending on the Diophantine properties of the rotation number. The $\theta$-intermediate dimension interpolates between these two dimensions. We use the well-understood gap structure of the irrational rotation map to develop a covering strategy to get upper bounds on the lower $\theta$-intermediate dimension, and use results of Banaji to show that these upper bounds are sharp for $\theta$ in an interval.
item.dc:creator: Milo Edwardes

item.title: Singular bifurcations in implicit discrete dynamical systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.12327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A periodic orbit of an implicit discrete system can persist when the implicit function theorem no longer guarantees a smooth successor. We develop a joint Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction of the periodic equations and the determinants marking singular transitions. In unrestricted smooth one-parameter families, the generic event is a single evolution fold on a continued orbit. Simultaneous normal forms describe its interactions with saddle-node and period-doubling bifurcations, locating the singular transitions and, under backward regularity, determining the diverging multipliers. The results cover arbitrary periods and periodically non-autonomous systems. Exact realisations and applications to labour-market equilibrium, machining and implicit integration illustrate the theory.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Buescu, Henrique M. Oliveira

item.title: Orbits along primes in totally minimal systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.12395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we show that every totally minimal system admits a point whose orbit along the primes is dense. Moreover, assuming the Dickson-Hardy-Littlewood conjecture, we show that in any totally minimal distal system, the orbit along the primes of every point is dense.
item.dc:creator: Wen Huang, Song Shao, Hui Xu, Xiangdong Ye

item.title: Singularities in leaf closures on complex surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.12402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a geometric and dynamical criterion excluding minimal sets contained in the regular locus of a holomorphic foliation on a compact complex surface. In particular, we prove that every Jouanolou foliation of degree at least two has no exceptional minimal set. We also give an explicit lower bound, growing linearly with the degree, for the number of singularities in every regular leaf closure of a Jouanolou foliation. This bound persists under small perturbations, as does the existence of a nonempty open saturated set whose leaves accumulate at all singularities. Under finite pullback unramified over the singular set, the bound is multiplied by the degree of the normalised component over the base leaf. Together with a general persistence theorem, this yields nonempty analytic open sets of foliations on every smooth projective surface with arbitrarily large uniform lower bounds on the number of singularities in their regular leaf closures. On double-plane K3 surfaces, we obtain foliations with ample canonical bundle and explicitly describe and count their singularities.
item.dc:creator: Mauricio Corr\^ea, Fernando Reis

item.title: Diophantine conditions for absolute continuity of projections for self-similar measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.12607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every projection of a planar self-similar measure $\mu$ is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on its support if the rotations satisfy a simultaneous Diophantine condition with exponent $\tau$ and $\mu$ has finite $s$-energy for some $1+2\tau\le s<2$. Under strong separation, we prove the fibre measures have exact dimension $\dim_H\mu-1$. For self-similar sets $E$ with $\dim_H E>1+2\tau$, the same rotation condition implies uniformly positive projection lengths and fibres of dimension $\dim_H E-1$ at Lebesgue-almost every point of each image without separation assumptions. The absolute continuity and fibre dimension theorems extend to non-coordinate projections of products under a joint Diophantine condition with exponent $\tau$ on the logarithmic contraction ratios. These imply for all self-similar sets $K,L\subset\mathbb R$ satisfying this condition and $\dim_HK+\dim_HL>1+2\tau$, every sum $uK+L$, $u\ne 0$, has positive length, and $\dim_H(L\cap(y-uK))=\dim_HK+\dim_HL-1$ for Leb. a.e. $y\in uK+L$. The proof combines the $L^1$ Gaussian smoothing approach used in the higher dimensional case with averaging at random stopping scales with a Brownian martingale bound using It\^{o} calculus.
item.dc:creator: Xiong Jin, Tuomas Sahlsten

item.title: Hidden frequencies in topological dynamical systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.12722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show for certain skew products built over any infinite minimal nilsystem, the frequencies present in the nilsystem are not always enough to govern recurrence for the whole system. This strengthens and generalizes a theorem of Glasscock, Koutsogiannis, and Richter.
item.dc:creator: Seljon Akhmedli

item.title: Residual-Based Spectral Submanifold Reduction of Constrained Multibody Systems on Matrix Lie Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.12726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The parameterization method yields efficient and accurate reduced-order models for nonlinear dynamical systems, but existing procedures that compute them assume polynomial vector fields on vector spaces. Constrained multibody systems instead obey differential-algebraic equations on matrix Lie groups such as $\mathbb{R}^3 \times SO(3)$ and $SE(3)$. Minimal parameterizations of these groups lead to non-polynomial equations that must be approximated or recast before reduction, and current implementations require the nonlinearities as explicit multilinear maps, which are cumbersome to construct for assembled multibody systems. This work develops a parameterization framework for constrained multibody systems on matrix Lie groups. Rigid and floating frame of reference bodies use rotation-matrix components or Euler parameters, while geometrically exact beam elements use an Euler-Rodrigues representation that eliminates the logarithmic map and expresses the exponential map polynomially, retaining screw-motion interpolation. The reduced-order models satisfy linear joint constraints exactly, and a rotation-preserving parameterization keeps the configuration on the Lie group to machine precision. The parameterization method is formulated directly in terms of the assembled residual, so that only residual evaluations and their derivatives are required. Truncated Taylor arithmetic delivers all Taylor coefficients of a given order from a single residual evaluation, and a non-intrusive coupling to codes with real-valued residuals is demonstrated with the multibody code Exudyn. Numerical examples show accurate prediction of backbone curves, forced response curves, and internal resonances at substantially reduced computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Holzinger, Tiago Martins, Daniel Rixen

item.title: Periodic vortex dipoles near closed geodesics on Riemannian surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.12743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the motion of a pair $(p_1,p_2)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma$ of point vortices with equal magnitude and opposite signs on a closed oriented Riemannian surface $(\Sigma,g)$. Given a closed geodesic that satisfies a non-degeneracy condition we construct a one-parameter family of periodic solutions $(p_1^\varepsilon,p_2^\varepsilon)$, $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$, of the Hamiltonian dynamical system for point vortex pairs whose trajectories converge towards the geodesic curve. The two vortices lie on opposite sides of the geodesic, are separated of order $\varepsilon$ and have period $2\pi\varepsilon$. The proof is based on a differentiated expansion of the Riemannian distance in Fermi coordinates, an augmented Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction, and an intricate contraction argument in scaled variables. The reduced normal equation is governed by the Jacobi operator of the closed geodesic, and the first order correction to the normal center of the dipole is characterized by an inhomogeneous Jacobi equation involving the curvature and the regular part of the Green function of the Laplace-Beltrami operator.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Bartsch, Angela Pistoia

item.title: The generic behavior of permutation entropy for continuous maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.12789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Permutation entropy, introduced by Bandt and Pompe in 2002, measures the complexity of a dynamical system through the ordinal patterns of its trajectories. Bandt, Keller and Pompe established that for measure-preserving, piecewise monotone interval maps with finitely many monotonicity intervals, the normalized order-$n$ permutation entropy $H_n^{\mathrm{perm}}(f)/n$ converges to the Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy. Although this result has subsequently been extended to broader classes of maps, whether normalized permutation entropy always converges has remained unknown. We show that convergence can fail, and indeed that nonconvergence is generic. More precisely, for a generic continuous Lebesgue measure-preserving map $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$, we prove that \[ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n^{\mathrm{perm}}(f)}{n}=0, \qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n^{\mathrm{perm}}(f)}{n\log n}=1. \] Thus, despite the generic vanishing of Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy, permutation entropy exhibits oscillations between vanishing linear growth and the maximal possible asymptotic growth. We also construct an explicit Lebesgue measure-preserving interval map with countably many monotonicity intervals for which the normalized permutation entropy has lower limit zero and upper limit infinity. This demonstrates that nonconvergence can occur even within the countably piecewise-monotone setting, beyond the scope of the convergence theorem of Gutjahr and Keller, relying on conditions concerning the lengths of the pieces.
item.dc:creator: Bal\'azs Maga, S\'ara Szepessy

item.title: Memory flows: geometry and dynamics of sequential retrieval in input-driven Hopfield networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.09995v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Associative memory models classically describe retrieval as convergence to stored patterns, but the theory of sequential retrieval remains comparatively limited. We develop a two-timescale input-driven Hopfield network in which fast associative retrieval is modulated by a slow feedback variable evolving over a prescribed memory-transition graph. This yields autonomous, graph-constrained transitions while preserving analytical tractability. Using slow-fast and geometric singular perturbation theory, we characterize memory fixation via memory manifolds and identify the geometric regions that govern stability loss and escape from retrieved memories. We further derive reduced slow dynamics and explicit criteria for transition onset, self-sustained retrieval, and collapse, expressed through escape times, gain thresholds, and fixed points. Together, these results provide a tractable framework for analyzing feedback-driven sequential retrieval in Hopfield networks.
item.dc:creator: Simone Betteti, Matteo Martin, Morten Gram Pedersen, Sandro Zampieri, Giacomo Baggio

item.title: Topological and measurewise amenability for locally compact groupoids
item.description: arXiv:2611.10010v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the equivalence of topological and measurewise amenability for $\sigma$-compact locally compact groupoids with a Hausdorff unit space and a continuous Haar system. This in particular includes the second countable locally compact Hausdorff case. Our proof averages arbitrary Radon probability measures along strictly positive densities to obtain quasi-invariant measures. We overcome the lack of absolute continuity of the original measure with respect to its quasi-invariant substitute by also averaging the Reiter functions along the same density.
item.dc:creator: Julian Kranz

item.title: On the dynamics of weighted shifts on Fr\'echet sequence spaces over trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.10053v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we give characterizations of Li--Yorke chaos, mean Li--Yorke chaos and distributional chaos for weighted backward shifts acting on general Fr\'echet sequence spaces over directed trees. As corollaries, we obtain explicit characterizations in the setting of K\"othe spaces $\lambda_p(A,V)$, where $p\in\{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ and $V$ is a directed tree. In particular, we obtain criteria for the case of the classical Banach spaces $\ell^p(V)$, $p\in[1,\infty)$, and $c_0(V)$.
item.dc:creator: Mateus Azevedo, Fernando Costa Jr., Jo\~ao V. A. Pinto

item.title: A singular homeomorphism between Pierce expansions and continued fraction expansions
item.description: arXiv:2611.10081v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the map $\Theta$ which sends each $x\in[0,1]$ to the number whose continued fraction digits are the first Pierce expansion digit of $x$ and the gaps between two consecutive Pierce expansion digits of $x$. We investigate the regularity of $\Theta$ and $\Theta^{-1}$, including the optimal H\"older exponent of $\Theta^{-1}$, and the local and Hausdorff dimensions of the push-forwards of the Lebesgue measure under $\Theta$ and $\Theta^{-1}$. We also study the differentiability of $\Theta$ at rational and irrational points, and calculate the Hausdorff dimension of the set of points at which $\Theta$ has an infinite derivative.
item.dc:creator: Min Woong Ahn

item.title: Turing Instability of a Closed Nutrient-Phytoplankton-Zooplankton-Detritus Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.10221v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Turing instability in a closed Nutrient-Phytoplankton-Zooplankton-Detritus (NPZD) ecosystem model with nutrient recycling, formulated as a reaction-diffusion system without an explicit time-delay. The detritus compartment represents the biomass during the recycling process and acts to introduce a time delay in this process. Total biomass in the system is conserved, leading to a closed model. Although spatial diffusion typically promotes stability, our focus is on understanding how different diffusion rates for different species can destabilize steady states and give rise to spatial patterns. To address this, we first perform linear stability analysis to identify conditions under which Turing instability may occur. We then validate these theoretical predictions through numerical simulations. Our approach develops both intuition and rigorous analysis of how diffusion influences instabilities in the context of a conservative system, offering a comprehensive framework for understanding pattern formation in multi-species plankton ecosystems.
item.dc:creator: Xiangye Xu, Sue Ann Campbell, Francis J. Poulin

item.title: Stability in the Non-Neutral and Neutral Regimes of the Holonomy-Based Inverse Problem in the Class \(\mathcal{OC}\)
item.description: arXiv:2611.10250v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study anchor reconstruction stability in return-map inverse problems for class $\mathcal O_C$. Local identifiability is governed by the first nonvanishing derivative of the holonomy map $H = T_\gamma - \text{Id}$. In the non-neutral case, we prove local Lipschitz stability and multiplier estimates. In the neutral regime, using Fa\`a di Bruno equations and Malgrange preparation, we derive quantitative $1/k$-H\"older estimates for order-$k$ anchor perturbations. We also establish finite jet stability, real-analytic dependence, and global $C^0$-stability of order $O(\varepsilon_F^{1/k})$. Numerical benchmarks on circular-core return geometries validate these theoretical convergence rates and square-root laws.
item.dc:creator: M. Barkatou, M. El Morsalani

item.title: Polynomial conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov maps derived from train track representatives
item.description: arXiv:2611.10381v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate two kinds of polynomials associated with pseudo-Anosov maps. Each kind consists of three polynomials that are conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes and these polynomials contain more information than pseudo-Anosov stretch factors. The first kind is defined by the train track representatives. The second kind is obtained from the first kind by incorporating additional data that encode the transitions among the unpunctured singularities of the invariant foliations. The Birman-Brinkmann-Kawamuro polynomials coincide with those of the second kind. As an application, we prove that the Birman-Brinkmann-Kawamuro polynomials are conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes which is also proved by Dodge-Kawamuro, independently.
item.dc:creator: Eiko Kin, Yuta Mizutani

item.title: Bulgarian solitaire with distinguishable cells
item.description: arXiv:2611.10437v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Classical Bulgarian solitaire tracks only the sizes of the stacks. We ask how the lengths of its periodic orbits change when individual cards are distinguished. To study this question, we introduce four actions $T_1,T_2,T_3,T_4$ on partitions with labeled cells. The actions differ in whether the top or bottom cell is removed from each column and in the order in which the removed cells are arranged to form a new column. We determine the exact sizes of the periodic orbits for all four actions. The main work lies in the analysis of $T_2$, for which we develop a coloring algorithm on Ferrers diagrams. The coloring encodes the cycle structure of the permutation of the labels induced by one full period of the underlying partition.
item.dc:creator: Vikum Bandara, Svetlana Poznanovi\'c

item.title: Confronting Uncertainty in Mechanism-AI Coupled Dynamical Systems via Optimal Transport and Information Geometry: Part I. Distribution Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.10563v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mechanism-AI coupled dynamical systems are increasingly used to study complex biological systems. However, uncertainty associated with noisy, sparse, and partially observed data limits their reliability. This paper presents a systematic mathematical formulation for treating these uncertainties from the perspective of optimal transport and information geometry. We formulate the uncertainty quantification problem as the minimization of an energy functional on a probability density space equipped with a Riemannian metric, with the loss evaluated through a differential equation, and give a unified description of the gradient flows of the energy functional under specific metrics, such as the Wasserstein and Fisher-Rao metrics. Furthermore, we present corresponding numerical methods for solving these gradient flows using abstract adjoint sensitivity analysis. The formulation connects a range of Bayesian inference methods for dynamical systems; numerical experiments compare posterior approximation and predictive uncertainty under a common computational budget. Moreover, it also provides a geometric perspective on dynamical modeling and the study of heterogeneity evolution.
item.dc:creator: Pengfei Song, Yanni Xiao, Shuangshuang Yin

item.title: Positivity Proofs for Third-Order Holonomic Sequences via Differences Scaled by Rational Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.10920v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the positivity of sequences $f$ that satisfy a third-order holonomic recurrence $f(n+3)= P_2(n) f(n+2) + P_1(n) f(n+1) + P_0(n) f(n)$ whose coefficients $P_0$, $P_1$ and $P_2$ are rational functions in $\R(x)$. We provide a sufficient condition on $P_0$, $P_1$ and $P_2$ for the recurrence to admit a solution all but finitely many terms of which are positive, and whose positivity is robust under small perturbations of the initial values. This sufficient condition is also a necessary condition for a subclass of the recurrences. By developing the proof of this sufficient condition, for another subclass of the recurrences, we show that it is decidable whether all the terms of a given sequence are positive for any initial values outside an exceptional plane. It is common to construct a positivity certificate, which guarantees the positivity of a solution, to show this kind of decidability. In this paper, we construct a new type of positivity certificate via the $S$-scaled difference $f(n+1) - S(n) f(n)$ for a suitable $S \in \R(x)$. This result partially improves the work by Ibrahim and Salvy.
item.dc:creator: Fugen Hagihara

item.title: Spectral gaps and mixing rates of primitive matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.10951v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain lower bounds on spectral gap/upper bounds for mixing rate for arbitrary $n$-state (not necessarily reversible) primitive Markov chains which have exponent $-O(n)$ rather than $-O(n^2)$, a significant improvement on the order obtained from classical arguments. Our improvements come from using the irreducibility distance and chainable index (which are at most linear in $n$) rather than the primitivity index (which can be near $n^2$). This also yields corresponding bounds for arbitrary nonnegative primitive matrices.
item.dc:creator: Solly Coles, Ronnie Pavlov

item.title: Mean-level arithmetic computation via stochastic reaction networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.11069v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reaction networks provide a natural model for analog computation in which inputs and outputs are encoded by molecular abundances. Much of the work on analog computation with chemical reaction networks (CRNs) has focused on deterministic mass-action systems. In DNA- and protein-based circuits, however, low copy numbers can make intrinsic fluctuations significant, motivating the use of stochastic models. In this paper, we develop a framework for computation with stochastic CRNs at the level of stationary means. Specifically, we construct elementary arithmetic modules for identification, addition, and multiplication, and analyze their mean-level correctness and convergence rates. We focus on these three modules because they are simple enough to analyze explicitly while already exhibiting the new issues raised by stochastic mean-level computation. Unlike in deterministic systems, the computed value cannot be read from a single output measurement. Instead, readout requires Monte Carlo estimation, with error arising from transient bias as the system approaches stationarity and intrinsic sampling noise that persists even at stationarity. We therefore study the convergence rates of output means, variances, and autocovariances to their stationary values, as well as the stationary fluctuations governing sampling error. We also show that this readout cost can depend strongly, and sometimes unexpectedly, on the architecture of the computation. In particular, comparing linear-chain and binary-tree implementations reveals that binary trees can greatly reduce stationary variance for addition, but can instead produce exponentially larger variance for multiplication.
item.dc:creator: David F. Anderson, Seokhwan Moon

item.title: K-PWM: Control-Oriented Structured Bilinear World Models under Partial Observation
item.description: arXiv:2611.11521v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World models learn internal simulators of environment dynamics for prediction, planning, and control, yet learning them from limited, noisy, and partial observations remains challenging. While much progress has focused on pixel-based observations, many physical systems instead provide vector-valued measurements that reveal only part of the underlying state. We introduce K-PWM, a probabilistic world model for prediction and control under partial observation. K-PWM couples Koopman-bilinear latent dynamics with a nonlinear observation decoder and performs probabilistic latent-state inference through the learned model via extended Kalman filtering and smoothing, without a separately trained inference network. Its bilinear structure enables exact propagation of the maintained Gaussian belief through the latent transition and efficient rollouts for uncertainty-aware model predictive path integral (MPPI) control. For training K-PWM, we present a generalized expectation conditional maximization (GECM) procedure with closed-form updates for the generators, noise covariances, and latent prior, complemented by gradient-based decoder learning. A Koopman-consistent initialization selects the latent dimension from data and initializes the action-dependent dynamics. With limited training data, K-PWM achieves lower long-horizon prediction error than the evaluated baselines on partially observed Gymnasium MuJoCo systems, while substantially reducing training time relative to the strongest prediction baseline. On high-dimensional MuJoCo Menagerie robots, it achieves competitive tracking accuracy with low per-step computation times, demonstrating potential for real-time deployment. These results support structured probabilistic dynamics as a data- and compute-efficient approach to world modeling and control under partial observation.
item.dc:creator: Santosh Mohan Rajkumar, Sriram Narayanan, Samuel E. Otto, Debdipta Goswami

item.title: Spectral Stability, Fatou Basin Contraction, and Machine-Checked Multipliers in Holomorphic Extensions of Generalized Syracuse Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.11641v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We embed the Syracuse operator $T(n) = n/2$ (even $n$), $T(n) = (3n+1)/2$ (odd $n$) and the Collatz map $C(n)$ into $\mathbb{C}$ via entire functions of exponential type $\pi$: $f(z) = \frac{1}{4}(1 + 4z - (1 + 2z)\cos(\pi z))$ and $F(z) = \frac{1}{4}(2 + 7z - (2 + 5z)\cos(\pi z))$. We prove five results: (1) every integer periodic cycle $C \subset \mathbb{N}^+$ of $T$ is a strictly attracting Fatou cycle of $f$ with multiplier $\mu_f(C) = 3^{N_{\mathrm{odd}}}/2^N = \prod_{n \in C\text{ odd}} \frac{3n}{3n+1} \in (0,1)$, and $\mu_f(O_{1,2}) = \mu_F(O_{1,4,2}) = 3/4 < 1$; (2) on the Fatou basin $B(O_{1,2})$, $g = f^{\circ 2}$ conjugates to $\Phi_j(g(z)) = \frac{3}{4}\Phi_j(z)$ with Koenigs Taylor jets $c_2(1) = -\frac{13}{2}\pi^2$ and $d_2(2) = -\frac{9}{2}\pi^2$; (3) the Schwarzian derivative is strictly negative on $\mathbb{Z}$ ($S(f)(n) \le 3\pi^2 - \frac{3}{8}\pi^4 \approx -6.9196 < 0$), and a repelling Julia 2-cycle $O_{\mathrm{rep}} \subset J(f)$ ($\mu \approx 1.2148 > 1$) isolates $B(O_{1,2})$; (4) on $(\mathbb{Z}_2, \mu_{\mathrm{Haar}})$, the 2-adic Lyapunov exponent $\lambda_{\mathrm{Haar}} = \frac{1}{2}\ln(3/4) \approx -0.143841 < 0$ equals $\frac{1}{2}\ln|\mu_f(O_{1,2})|$; and (5) we certify 20 theorems in Lean 4 (anc/CollatzAttractor.lean, 0 sorry). These results establish local Fatou invariants and 2-adic ergodic averages for $f(z)$, leaving open whether every $n_0 \in \mathbb{N}^+$ lies in $\bigcup_{k \ge 0} f^{-k}(B(O_{1,2}))$.
item.dc:creator: Volkan Da\u{g}l{\i}, Zerrin Da\u{g}l{\i}, Da\u{g}han Da\u{g}l{\i}, Emrah Yurtseven, Murat Emre \"Ozkaya

item.title: Data-Driven Precision Control of Soft Helicoid Robots
item.description: arXiv:2611.11709v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A purely data-driven method grounded in the theory of adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs) was recently used to model and control nonlinear soft robotic simulators. Here, we extend the methodology to learn aSSM-reduced models from data collected from hardware soft robotic platforms. Specifically, we learn a five dimensional (5D) aSSM-reduced nonlinear ordinary differential equation (ODE) that accurately models the dynamics of a soft-helicoid trunk robot. We then use this ODE in a model predictive control scheme to demonstrate real-time precision control across various challenging closed-loop trajectory-tracking tasks, ranging from 2D to 3D trajectories with static and dynamic constraints. We find that our methodology enhances accuracy and precision across all control tasks compared to available data-driven linear methods and model-free reinforcement learning. While we focus here on a soft-helicoid trunk robot, our methodology relies solely on hardware data and is therefore applicable to a broader class of soft robotic systems.
item.dc:creator: Roshan S. Kaundinya, Mark Leone, Roberto Sabella, Hugo Buurmeijer, Luis Pabon, John Irvin Alora, Marco Pavone, George Haller

item.title: Accelerated Reinforcement Learning for Soft Robotics: Hours Instead of Years
item.description: arXiv:2611.11718v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) requires large amounts of interaction data or a reliable simulator, both hard to obtain for nonlinear soft robotic hardware. Recent work shows that a time-scale separation inherent to soft robot dynamics justifies their reduction to low-dimensional invariant manifolds, known as adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs). We demonstrate that an aSSM-reduced model, a simple polynomial ordinary differential equation learned purely from pre-collected data, can serve as an RL training environment. On a pneumatically actuated soft arm, we train a trajectory-tracking policy in 3 hours on a six-dimensional aSSM-reduced model and deploy it without fine-tuning, whereas reproducing this policy training extrapolates to 3 years of hardware interaction. Our policy tracks dynamic targets with 40% lower error than otherwise identical policies trained on a 4.8-million-parameter recurrent neural network (RNN) or a 1.7-million-parameter transformer, which take 13 and 100 hours to identify, against 5 minutes for our mathematically justified 6,924-parameter model.
item.dc:creator: Roshan S. Kaundinya, Hehui Zheng, Robert K. Katzschmann, George Haller

item.title: Operator Learning of Microstructure-Dependent Internal-Variable Models for Inelastic Homogenization: Approximation and Complexity
item.description: arXiv:2611.11805v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the learning of homogenized constitutive laws for inelastic heterogeneous materials, aiming to replace costly concurrent unit-cell simulations with surrogates that generalize across loading histories and microstructures. We focus on the recurrent neural operator framework, motivated by the explicit form of homogenized Kelvin--Voigt linear viscoelasticity. In this framework, internal variables enable a Markovian approximation of loading-history dependence, and neural operators represent the microstructure-dependent constitutive response. For periodic Kelvin--Voigt viscoelasticity, we prove a universal approximation theorem showing that the model can approximate the homogenized constitutive law to any prescribed accuracy, uniformly in time and over a wide set of admissible strain trajectories and microstructural property fields, in two and three dimensions. This comprises a significant extension of the existing, somewhat limited, one-dimensional theory that uses explicit solutions for piecewise constant materials. Instead, in two and three dimensions, we adopt a more versatile approximation based on the spectral representation of the memory kernel that arises from homogenization. This also enables us to give an explicit bound on the internal-variable dimension, sufficient for approximation, exhibiting logarithmic growth in the inverse relative stress error and in material contrast. Numerical experiments on viscoelasticity and crystal plasticity complement the theory, illustrating the roles of internal-variable dimension and sample complexity in learning homogenized responses from unit-cell data. Theoretical results are formally verified in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Lianghao Cao, George Stepaniants, Andrew M. Stuart

item.title: Integrable Measure Equivalence and Gromov's conjecture on nilpotent groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.12009v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article we prove a well-known conjecture due to M. Gromov that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Quasi-isometric, then their Mal'cev Completions are isomorphic as Lie groups. We prove this result in more general set-up. We prove that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent, then the Mal'cev completions of $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Equivalently, using Y. Shalom's result we prove that two infinite countable torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent if and only if $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are quasi-isometric if and only if the Mal'cev Completions of $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Moreover, we discuss some applications of our main theorem to lifting of quasi-isometric embedding from $\Gamma$ to $\Lambda$ to a homo-morphism between their Mal'cev completions, and betti numbers of nilpotent groups.
item.dc:creator: Kajal Das

item.title: A Finite-Lag Markov Chain Model for Coarse-Graining Linear SDEs
item.description: arXiv:2611.12022v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we analyze a finite-lag Markov chain approximation for coarse-grained linear stochastic differential equations. The chain uses the limiting conditional transition law of the resolved variables to advance on a prescribed time grid. Its stability and statistical properties are studied, with particular attention to the role of the lag time. The chain preserves the exact equilibrium distribution and matches the autocovariance at the chosen lag, while errors at subsequent times are quantified. For a slow-fast system, the analysis relates lag selection to scale separation and dynamical accuracy. A continuous embedding of the chain enables a unified comparison with some existing continuous-time Markovian effective models based on the temporal statistics they preserve. Numerical examples illustrate the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Chen

item.title: Lie-Lions brackets of nonlocal vector fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.12108v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study nonlocal vector fields on the space of probability measures with finite second moment. Using Lions derivatives, we define their Lie-Lions bracket, which adds to the spatial Lie bracket a correction due to the evolution of the law, and prove that its vanishing is equivalent to commutation of the global flows, under first-order regularity and linear growth assumptions. We then construct a Lie algebra of complete polynomial nonlocal fields. For this class, we establish commutator and second-order Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formulas with cubic remainders in the Wasserstein distance $W_2$, controlled by the second moment and uniform in the number of particles. The proofs rely on finite-particle realizations, which preserve the bracket and jointly determine the nonlocal field. We also obtain uniform estimates for smooth bounded kernels and a Leibniz rule for the action of polynomial fields on polynomial observables. Examples from collective dynamics show that the vanishing of the spatial bracket at a fixed law is neither necessary nor sufficient for commutation. They concern symmetries, aggregation-dependent rotation, synchronization, the transmission of a turn along a hierarchy, effective three-body interactions and occupancy-dependent circulation.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Boulard, Amaury Hayat, Benedetto Piccoli, Emmanuel Tr\'elat

item.title: The balance between feature learning and collapse in dynamical systems-based generative models
item.description: arXiv:2611.12156v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Over the past decade, a growing body of work has established that implicit biases in learning dynamics fundamentally shape the solutions found by neural networks, governing their learned features and generalisation performance. However, despite these strides in deep learning theory, far less is known about representation learning in generative models based on dynamical systems, from normalising flows to diffusion. Importantly, empirical evidence suggests that continuous-time generative models can be prone to mode collapse, yet a learning theory explaining such biases remains elusive. To address this, we use tools from dynamical systems and operator theory to express the gradient flow of a general class of stochastic differential equations as a composition of linear operators, allowing us to relate collapse to low-rank biases in generative models. In variational inference and flow-matching tasks, we show that this bias can manifest in two different mechanisms: i) where collapsed models are stable fixed points of the gradient flow, or ii) in sequential feature learning, where smaller modes take progressively longer to be learned, producing an effective collapse for a fixed training budget. Together these findings point to a trade-off between feature learning and collapse, suggesting an operator view as a step towards a unified framework for understanding the learning dynamics of dynamical systems-based generative models.
item.dc:creator: Julian Brandon, Bruno Loureiro, N Alex Cayco-Gajic, Arthur Pellegrino

item.title: Reconstructing Flash-Evoked Potentials in the Human Brain and Tracking Cortical Activity Using Spatiotemporal Filtering: Numerical Simulation Study
item.description: arXiv:2611.12366v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electroencephalographic source reconstruction of visual evoked activity is challenging because distributed, temporally evolving, and overlapping cortical sources generate scalp potentials. We present a controlled simulation framework for flash visual evoked potentials (FVEPs) based on a coupled Jansen--Rit neural mass network and a realistic finite-element EEG forward model. The framework generates a sequential activation pattern across early visual, parietal, and frontal regions and enables direct comparison of reconstructed activity with known ground truth. Standardized Kalman filtering (SKF), change-rate SKF (CrSKF), conventional Kalman filtering (KF), and linearly constrained minimum variance (LCMV) beamforming are compared using parcel-wise time courses, temporal lags, and assessments of spatial focality and Earth Mover's Distance. In the inverse comparison, SKF and CrSKF preserve the principal temporal progression more consistently than KF and LCMV, while CrSKF produces smoother temporal estimates. The results also demonstrate parcel-wise leakage and reduced separation of closely spaced components, emphasizing the need to interpret temporal ordering together with spatial reconstruction quality. The proposed framework provides a reproducible test environment for evaluating dynamic EEG inverse methods under controlled noise conditions.
item.dc:creator: Qiong Tao, Joonas Lahtinen, Sampsa Pursiainen

item.title: Converse Lyapunov theorem for input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.12601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove converse Lyapunov theorems for input-to-state stability (ISS) of a broad class of infinite-dimensional systems applicable to evolution equations in Banach spaces, boundary control systems, and delay systems. To this end, we employ a novel method that does not require constructing auxiliary closed-loop systems. We start by showing that ISS of a control system implies uniform global asymptotic stability of the same system with respect to trajectory-dominated inputs. Then, under an additional regularity requirement, we prove that an ISS Lyapunov function can be constructed. Based on our general result, we prove that for linear systems with unbounded $\infty$-admissible operators, ISS is equivalent to the existence of a Lipschitz continuous coercive ISS Lyapunov function.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Bachmann, Andrii Mironchenko

item.title: Hamiltonian Cotangent Deformations of Space Forms: Curvature Pinching, Soliton Rigidity, Conjugate Loci, and Superintegrability
item.description: arXiv:2611.12821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the one-parameter family of Riemannian metrics $g_\lambda$ induced by the Hamiltonian cotangent deformation $H_\lambda = H_0 + \frac{\lambda}{2}\|J\|^2$ on simply connected space forms of constant curvature $\kappa \in \{1, 0, -1\}$, where $J$ is the momentum map of the isotropy action fixing a base point. The master reciprocal identity $1/f_\lambda^2 = 1/s_\kappa^2 + \lambda$ governing the warping function controls the geometry of the family and implies that radial geodesic acceleration is independent of $\lambda$. From this mechanism we derive three classes of results: (1) Curvature and rigidity: closed-form sectional curvatures, the sharp positivity trichotomy, pointwise and global Brendle-Schoen $1/4$-pinching windows on $\mathbb{S}^{n+1}$, never-Einstein rigidity for $\lambda \neq 0$, and the realization of Hamilton's steady cigar soliton on $(\mathbb{H}^2, g_1)$ as the unique gradient Ricci soliton in the family. (2) Dynamics and stability: iso-kinematic decoupling into unperturbed radial motion and uniform precession $\Omega = \lambda L$, closed-form Clairaut integration, the transcendental inward conjugate point law with Euclidean inversion $r_0 R^* = 1/\lambda$, and stratified $A_3$ cusp caustics. (3) Integrability and spectral theory: maximal superintegrable rational pericenter invariants on $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, transverse Killing rigidity on curved space forms, Fuchsian Heun spectral reduction with modulus $\tau = 1 + \lambda/\kappa$, and essential spectrum gap collapse to $[0, \infty)$ on $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}$. Extensions to anisotropic sphere families and intrinsic deformations of compact rank-one symmetric spaces ($\mathbb{C}P^n, \mathbb{H}P^n, \mathbb{O}P^2$) are also established.
item.dc:creator: James J. Munden

item.title: Hamiltonian Cotangent Deformations and Closed-Form Geodesics on Non-Naturally Reductive Orbit Spheres: The Spin(9) 15-Sphere and the Cayley Plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.12828v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: By the Skew-Torsion Holonomy Theorem of Olmos and Reggiani (2012), the 15-sphere $S^{15}$ admits no non-trivial naturally reductive metric under any transitive Lie group, precluding geodesic integration via canonical Ambrose-Singer connections. Simultaneously, Nikonorov (2013) established that every $Spin(9)$-invariant metric on $S^{15}$ is a geodesic orbit (GO) space. We integrate the geodesic flow on this non-naturally reductive GO manifold via the Lie Subalgebra Closure Principle: whenever the slice generators of a multi-axial reductive decomposition close into a finite-rank reductive Lie subalgebra, the geodesic vector equations decouple into an algebraic eigenvalue problem. Using the 16-dimensional spin representation and Vol'per's decomposition $\mathfrak{spin}(9) = \mathfrak{spin}(7) \oplus \mathfrak{p}_1 \oplus \mathfrak{p}_2$, we prove that the slice generators $X_1 \in \mathfrak{p}_2$ and $Y_1 \in \mathfrak{p}_1$ close into $\mathfrak{u}(2) \cong \mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1) \subset \mathfrak{so}(16)$. The generator $M = \alpha X_1 + \beta Y_1$ has the four-mode spectrum $\Omega \in \{ |R \pm 3\alpha|, |R \pm \alpha| \}$ ($R = \sqrt{\alpha^2 + \beta^2}$), yielding a closed-form 4-projector decomposition and Euler-Cartan factorization for $\exp(\alpha X_1 + \beta Y_1)$. Under the normalized Ricci flow, we prove that the Bourguignon-Karcher squashed Einstein metric at $t = 3/11$ ($\lambda = 64$) is an unstable repeller separating sub-Riemannian fiber collapse from the round sphere basin. Finally, on the deformed Cayley plane $\mathbb{O}P^2 = F_4/Spin(9)$, we prove universal CROSS never-Einstein rigidity, establish the 15-dimensional three-stratum Whitney stratification of the cut locus $Cut(q_0)$ at non-polar basepoints $q_0$, and prove Blaschke and Besse rigidity for all $\lambda > 0$.
item.dc:creator: James J. Munden

item.title: Topologically transitive semigroup actions of real linear fractional transformations
item.description: arXiv:0908.3316v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $F_I=\{f:I\to I \mid f(x)=(Ax+B)/(Cx+D),\ AD-BC\neq 0\}$, where $I$ is a proper closed subinterval of $\mathbb{R}$. We describe all pairs $f,g\in F_I$ for which the action of the semigroup $\langle f,g \rangle$ generated by $f$ and $g$ is topologically transitive on $I$. It turns out that for such pairs topological transitivity, hypercyclicity, and density of every interior orbit are equivalent. Using the Hilbert metric of $I$ we show that no subsemigroup of $F_I$, with any number of generators, acts in a weakly topologically mixing way on $I$. We classify the pairs of affine maps of $\mathbb{R}$ whose semigroup action is topologically transitive, weakly topologically mixing, or hypercyclic, and we show that such an action is never $3$-transitive. In contrast, there are pairs of real linear fractional transformations whose semigroup action on $\mathbb{R}$ is topologically $3$-transitive, while no semigroup of linear fractional transformations is $4$-transitive.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, Topologically transitive semigroup actions of real linear fractional transformations, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 368 (2010), 587--603
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: Hilbert number for a family of piecewise nonautonomous equations
item.description: arXiv:2307.15578v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For family $x'=(a_0+a_1\cos t+a_2\sin t)|x|+b_0+b_1\cos t+b_2\sin t$, we solve three basic problems related with its dynamics. First, we characterize when it has a center (Poincar\'e center focus problem). Second, we show that each equation has a finite number of limit cycles (finiteness problem), and finally we give a uniform upper bound for the number of limit cycles (Hilbert problem 16).
item.dc:creator: J. L. Bravo, M. Fern\'andez, I. Ojeda

item.title: Heat equation from a deterministic dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2310.13338v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive the heat equation for the thermal energy under diffusive space-time scaling for a purely deterministic microscopic dynamics satisfying Newton equations perturbed by an external chaotic force acting like a magnetic field.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: G. Canestrari, C. Liverani, S. Olla, Heat equation from a deterministic dynamics. Invent. math. 245, 1437--1504 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Canestrari, Carlangelo Liverani, Stefano Olla

item.title: New Obstacles to Multiple Recurrence
item.description: arXiv:2511.21680v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that there is a set which is not a set of multiple recurrence despite being a set of recurrence for nil-Bohr sets. This answers Huang, Shao, and Ye's "higher-order" version of Katznelson's Question on Bohr recurrence and topological recurrence in the negative. Equivalently, we construct a set $S$ so that there is a finite coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ without monochromatic three-term arithmetic progressions with common differences in $S$, but so that $S$ lacks the usual polynomial obstacles to arithmetic progressions. This represents a significant contribution to our understanding of when a restricted van der Waerden theorem or a restricted Szemer\'edi Theorem holds, an important problem in additive combinatorics and Ramsey theory.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Alweiss

item.title: Transient rebellions in the Kuramoto oscillator: Morse-Smale structural stability and connection graphs of finite 2-shift type
item.description: arXiv:2512.02937v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The celebrated 1975 Kuramoto model of $N$ identical oscillators with phase angle vector $\boldsymbol{\vartheta}=(\vartheta_1,\ldots,\vartheta_N)$ and all-to-all coupling reads \begin{equation} \label{*} \dot\vartheta_j\,=\tfrac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^N \sin(\vartheta_k-\vartheta_j). \tag{*} \end{equation} Here we have passed to co-rotating coordinates in normalized time scale. The model is highly accessible to rigorous mathematical analysis, and has been studied as a paradigm for effects like total and partial synchronization. Most initial conditions $\boldsymbol{\vartheta}$ lead to total synchronization. The large number of asymptotically $\sim 2^{N-1}$ (circles of) partially synchronized states, however, is unstable. The precise behavior of transitions to synchrony seems to have eluded description. In the present paper, we address this gap. By the gradient structure of (*), the global dynamics decompose into equilibria and heteroclinic orbits between them. Except for the extremes of total instability and total synchrony, all equilibria are 2-cluster solutions: their phase angles $\vartheta_j$ attain only two values, with a phase difference of $\pi$ between them. Any heteroclinic orbit between 2-cluster equilibria, or towards synchrony, can be realized as a 3-cluster rebellion. Cluster rebellions split the smaller, "slim", minority cluster of the source equilibrium and send the rebellious part to join the bigger, "fat", majority cluster. Heteroclinic transversality identifies the Kuramoto model as a structurally stable Morse-Smale system. In particular, heteroclinic orbits can be concatenated in finite time. The options involved in successive cluster rebellions amount to finite symbol sequences of 2-shift type. We include numerical illustrations, and a comparison with coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators. The paper is dedicated to Professor Yoshiki Kuramoto, with admiration.
item.dc:creator: Jia-Yuan Dai, Bernold Fiedler, Alejandro L\'opez-Nieto

item.title: Piecewise Smooth Dynamical Systems Regularized by Convolution
item.description: arXiv:2601.00697v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a general regularization procedure for piecewise smooth vector fields whose discontinuity locus is a variety of normal crossings type. We show that such regularization can be smoothed through a finite sequence of blowings-up, thereby reducing the problem to the study of the dynamics of a smooth vector field in a manifold with corners. The procedure will be illustrated in the cases of piecewise smooth vector fields on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with discontinuity locus $x=0$ or $xy=0$, and on $\mathbb{R}^3$ with discontinuity locus $xyz=0$. We will see that some unexpected dynamical phenomena such as Bogdanov-Takens bifurcations and Bykov cycles may arise even in the case of piecewise constant vector fields.
item.dc:creator: Claudio A. Buzzi, Daniel Panazzolo, Paulo R. da Silva

item.title: Phase transitions on periodic orbits in $\beta$-transformation with a hole at zero
item.description: arXiv:2602.05438v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given $\beta\in(1,2]$, let $T_\beta: [0,1)\to[0,1);~x\mapsto\beta x\pmod 1$. For $m\in\mathbb N$ let \[ \tau_m(\beta):=\sup\left\{t\in[0,1): K_\beta(t)\textrm{ contains a periodic orbit of smallest period }m \right\}, \] where $K_\beta(t)=\{x\in[0,1): T_\beta^n(x)\notin(0,t)~\forall n\ge 0\}$ is the survivor set of the open dynamical system $(T_\beta, [0,1), H)$ with a hole $H=(0,t)$. In this paper we give a complete characterization of $\tau_m$, and show that $\tau_m$ is piecewise continuous with precisely $\psi(m)$ discontinuity points, where $\psi(m)$ is the number of bulbs of period $m$ in the Mandelbrot set. To describe the critical value function $\tau_m$ we construct a finite butterfly tree $\mathcal T_m$, from which we are able to determine the discontinuity points and the analytic formula of $\tau_m$ based on Farey words and substitution operators. As a by product, we characterize the extremal Lyndon words and extremal Perron words. Since we are working in the symbolic space, our result can be applied to study phase transitions for periodic orbits in topologically expansive Lorenz maps, doubling map with an asymmetric hole, intermediate $\beta$-transformations, unique expansions in double bases, and so on.
item.dc:creator: Derong Kong, Dantong Pu

item.title: A universal model for the bifurcations of asymptotic values
item.description: arXiv:2603.15466v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a universal model for the bifurcation of asymptotic values, based on the notion of tangent-like maps and families thereof. In analogy with polynomials and polynomial-like maps, we prove that every tangent-like map can be associated to a member of the model family. In particular, the filled Julia sets of tangent-like maps are quasiconformally homeomorphic to the ones for the model family. Likewise, the bifurcation locus of a family of tangent-like maps is homeomorphic to the boundary of the {\em Tandelbrot set} $\mathcal T$, the bifurcation locus of the model. Moreover $\mathcal T$ is universal, in the sense that homeomorphic copies of it can be found densely in the activity loci of asymptotic values of any appropriate natural family of finite type meromorphic maps. When applied to the iterates of a transcendental meromorphic map, these results make it possible to build a transcendental renormalization theory, a question that has been open for the last 25 years.
item.dc:creator: Matthieu Astorg, Anna Miriam Benini, N\'uria Fagella

item.title: Induced fiber topological pressure for random dynamical systems
item.description: arXiv:2604.14964v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce induced fiber topological pressure for random dynamical systems and identify it with two critical exponents and the threshold of classical fiber pressure, allowing infinite fiber topological entropy. We establish an almost-sure fiberwise formula and a variational principle, and identify induced equilibrium states with classical equilibrium states. If the fiber topological entropy is finite and the entropy map is upper semicontinuous, an ergodic induced equilibrium state exists.
item.dc:creator: Cunyi Nan

item.title: On the construction of almost periodic solutions for the derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2604.23202v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we consider a derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation $$ \mathrm{i}\partial_{t}u+\partial_{xx}u-V\ast u+\mathrm{i}\vert u\vert^{2}\partial_{x}u=0 $$ on the torus $\mathbb{T}$, depending on some potential $V$. We prove that for `almost all' potentials $V$, this equation admits an almost-periodic solution.
item.dc:creator: Yuchen WU, Xiaoping Yuan

item.title: Orbital Networks in the Three-Body Problem
item.description: arXiv:2605.31543v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Orbital transfers in multi-body systems are often studied as isolated trajectory design problems, making it difficult to identify the larger transport structure connecting families of periodic orbits, including which families act as hubs, gateways, relays, or persistently difficult-to-access regions. This work introduces a reachable-set-based framework for constructing orbital networks in the circular restricted three-body problem.
