Finite-$\Delta V$ and finite-time-of-flight reachable-set overlaps are used to infer accessibility relationships between representative periodic orbit families on a common Jacobi energy manifold and to assemble these relationships into a weighted orbital network. Applied to the Earth-Moon system, the resulting network reveals distinct accessibility regimes in which direct reachability, graph connectedness, and feasible multileg closure emerge separately. The analysis identifies multi-orbiter cycler orbits as the dominant hub, gateway, and relay families, with the (3,2)-cycler dominating across much of the sampled budget plane and the short-period (1,1)-cycler dominating in the low-time-of-flight regime, while the stable 2:1 resonant orbit remains persistently difficult to access. Although the maximum-budget network is nearly complete in a binary sense, its weighted accessibility remains strongly non-uniform. Selected proxy-supported connections are refined into concrete trajectories through differential correction, with corrected transfer costs remaining below the proxy estimates in all tested cases. Together, the results demonstrate how reachable-set overlap geometry can expose large-scale transport structure in nonlinear gravitational systems without requiring exhaustive pairwise trajectory optimization.
item.dc:creator: Abdullah Braik, Shane D. Ross

item.title: A Note on Singular Boundary Regularisation in Hamiltonian Systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.09952v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Singular changes of variables in Hamiltonian systems, such as McGehee coordinates in celestial mechanics or renormalised variables in dispersive PDE blow-up, are designed to extend the equations of motion to a singular boundary. In contrast, it may be that near the boundary, the the induced symplectic two-form may rescale distinct geometric directions by distinct powers of the singular scale, and if the leading weighted part is degenerate, no single conformal factor makes the form extend as a smooth non-degenerate two-form. This anisotropic obstruction is complementary to the isotropic singularities studied in bm-symplectic geometry. We record it in an elementary finite-dimensional criterion and illustrate it with McGehee regularisation of homogeneous central-force collisions and, formally, with the modulation geometry of focusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation blow-up.
item.dc:creator: Cristina Stoica

item.title: Abundance of typical horseshoes for the random standard map
item.description: arXiv:2609.12908v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a notion of typical horseshoe, consisting of a pair of rectangles admitting Markov returns at times of positive lower density, with controlled hyperbolic geometry and orbits that shadow typical trajectories. We prove the abundance of typical horseshoes for the random standard map and establish several statistical properties of the system, including exponential mixing and large deviation estimates for the associated projective and two-point processes.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe Tenaglia

item.title: Sharp iterated-logarithmic thresholds for quantitative measure and orbit equivalence between integer lattices
item.description: arXiv:2609.15816v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We identify the sharp iterated-logarithmic thresholds at the critical exponent for quantitative measure equivalence and orbit equivalence between integer lattices. To be more precise, let $n>m$ be two positive integers, $\alpha$ be a positive number and $( \beta_j)_{j \geqslant 1}$ be a finitely supported sequence of non-negative numbers. We show that there is a quantitatively $t^{\alpha}\cdot \prod_{j \geqslant 1} ( \log^{(j)}{t} )^{-\beta_j} $-integrable measure equivalence from $\mathbb{Z}^n$ to $\mathbb{Z}^m$ if and only if either $\alpha<m/n$ or $\alpha=m/n$ and there is $j_* \geqslant 1$ such that $\beta_j= 1$ for all $1 \leqslant j < j_*$ and $\beta_{j_*} > 1$. Here $\log^{(j)}$ is the $j$-fold iterated logarithm. The same characterization holds for quantitative orbit equivalence. This characterization greatly strengthens the previous best-known result, due to the work of Delabie, Koivisto, Le Ma\^itre and Tessera (2022) and the work of Correia (2025), which asserts that there is a $t^{\alpha}$-integrable ($\alpha>0$) measure equivalence (or orbit equivalence) from $\mathbb{Z}^n$ to $\mathbb{Z}^m$ if and only if $\alpha<m/n$. In particular, our result solves, in much stronger forms, two open problems posed respectively by Delabie, Koivisto, Le Ma\^itre and Tessera, and by Naryshkin and Petrakos.
item.dc:creator: Changhua Jiao

item.title: Weighted averages and applications to sets of multiple recurrence
item.description: arXiv:2609.16554v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce new techniques for determining combinatorial properties of sets of multiple recurrence by considering weighted averages with quickly growing weights. Our main result is a far-reaching generalization of Szemer\'edi's Theorem which additionally confirms a conjecture of Bergelson-Moreira-Richter and contains as special cases both a variant of the Polynomial Szemer\'edi Theorem due to Bergelson-Leibman-Lesigne and the fact that if $f$ belongs to a broad class of smooth functions and satisfies $x^{d-1}\prec f(x)\prec x^d$ for some $d\in \mathbb{N}$ then for any $\ell\in \mathbb{N}$, any invertible measure preserving system $(X,\mathscr{B},\mu,T)$, and any $A\in \mathscr{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, the set $\{n\in \mathbb{N}: \mu(A\cap T^{-[f(n)]}A\cap T^{-2[f(n)]}A\cap \cdots\cap T^{-\ell[f(n)]}A )>0\}$ is thick, meaning that it contains arbitrarily long intervals of natural numbers. Additionally, we formulate and prove a generalization to weighted averages of Boshernitzan's criterion for uniform distribution which we use in the proof of our main result.
item.dc:creator: Vitaly Bergelson, Michael Reilly

item.title: On normal forms and first integrals of planar maps at elliptic fixed points
item.description: arXiv:2609.21417v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study real-analytic, planar, maps, at a neighbourhood of an elliptic fixed point. We construct normal forms for them, when they admit a real-analytic first integral. We prove that a second first integral, when it exists, forces their linearisation. We consider both the resonant and the non-resonant case, whether the maps preserve a symplectic form or not. The second first integral is allowed to be smooth, real-meromorphic or real-analytic.
item.dc:creator: Stavros Anastassiou

item.title: Sectorial normalisation of one resonant biholomorphisms near a fixed point
item.description: arXiv:2609.24695v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we study germs of biholomorphisms of $(\C^n,0)$, $n\geq 2$ fixing the origin, the linear part at which has all its eigenvalues on the unit circle. We prove the existence of a {\it sectorial} transformation to a polynomial normal form of a non-degenerate 1-resonant biholomorphism under a Diophantine condition. We also give their holomorphic classification. We show that the {\it sectorial} automorphisms of the polynomial normal form are {\it exponentially flat} perturbations of the identity. We deduce the Gevrey character of the formal normalizing transformation and we show how the Gevrey index depends on the Diophantine exponent.
item.dc:creator: Maxime Chatal (CNRS,UniCA), Laurent Stolovitch (CNRS,UniCA)

item.title: No infinite spin in the $n$-body problem in all dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2609.33250v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the planar $n$-body problem, Moeckel and Montgomery \cite{MM25} showed that there is no infinite spin for total collision solutions, when the reduced and normalized configuration converges to an isolated central configuration. Following their approach, generalizations have been obtained for partial collision solutions and parabolic solutions in the planar case, and for total collision solutions in the spatial cases by various authors, all under the same assumption that the reduced and normalized configuration converges to an isolated central configuration. Here we prove there is no infinite spin for any collision or parabolic solution in all dimensions without such an assumption.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Wang, Guowei Yu

item.title: Discontinuous actions of rational special linear groups on manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.15653v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every $n\geq 1$, we construct continuum-many pairwise non-conjugate actions of $\operatorname{SL}(n+1,\mathbb{Q})$ by homeomorphisms on the $n$-sphere. None of these actions extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}(n+1,\mathbb{R})$. Our construction refines a blow-up procedure of Bowden and Mann, allowing the stabiliser action inside each blown-up disc to be prescribed. We motivate studying these actions and record some related observations.
item.dc:creator: Segev Gonen Cohen

item.title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.29211v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that for every open $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $\theta(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb{R}$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field. Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. We extend our conclusions from the Euclidean metric to a general class of ambient metrics including Riemannian metrics and we establish uniform local upper bounds for the lengths of the spherical projections of gradient flow trajectories. We finally apply our findings to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).
item.dc:creator: Thang Do, Arnulf Jentzen, Benno Kuckuck

item.title: The convergence-divergence criterion for the Ma\~n\'e cohomology lemma and Liv\v{s}ic theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.32484v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a dynamical convergence-divergence criterion for all functions with a prescribed modulus of continuity to have continuous sub-actions. The divergence part of the criterion, which gives functions that do not have any bounded sub-action, is valid for general dynamical systems with a weakly repelling fixed point. This unifies and generalises versions of the Ma\~n\'e cohomology lemma for uniformly expanding maps, and results of Morris for maps with an indifferent fixed point. One consequence is that for any infinite compact metric space $(X,\rho)$, and Lipschitz Ruelle-expanding map $T:X\to X$, a metric transform $\omega$ satisfies Dini's criterion $\int_0 \omega(s)s^{-1}\, ds <\infty$ if and only if all functions that are Lipschitz for $\omega\circ\rho$ have continuous sub-actions. Another consequence is that if $T$ is an expanding circle map of Manneville--Pomeau type $\alpha\in(0,1)$, then $\omega$ satisfies the convergence criterion $\int_0 \omega(s)s^{-1-\alpha}\, ds <\infty$ if and only if all functions that are Lipschitz for $\omega\circ\rho$ have continuous sub-actions. For the latter class of maps, with $\omega$ satisfying the convergence criterion, we prove a Liv\v{s}ic theorem for functions $f$ that are Lipschitz for $\omega\circ\rho$: if $\int f\, d\mu=0$ for all invariant measures $\mu$, then $f=\varphi\circ T-\varphi$ for a function $\varphi$ that is Lipschitz with respect to $D_\alpha(\omega)\circ\rho$, where $D_\alpha(\omega)(t)= \int_0^t \omega(s)s^{-1-\alpha}\, ds$.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Jenkinson, Yiwei Zhang, Hang Zhao

item.title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems I: The Half-Plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.01014v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, the first in a series devoted to finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in domains with boundaries, we investigate finite-time boundary collisions and interior collapse for three vortices in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}^+$. We first prove that finite-time boundary collisions are impossible for arbitrary nonzero vortex circulations, without any restrictions on their signs or algebraic relations. The result excludes both simultaneous boundary collapse and individual vortex approaches to the boundary, without requiring convergence of the vortex trajectories. In contrast, we establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse by treating the boundary-induced interactions as a perturbation of the classical self-similar Gr\"{o}bli collapse in the full plane. Under suitable conditions on the vortex circulations and collapse profile, we prove the existence of a one-dimensional local strong stable manifold of the augmented rescaled system, which generates exact solutions in which three distinct vortices collapse simultaneously at any prescribed interior point $z^*\in\mathbb{H}^+$. Moreover, these solutions are asymptotically self-similar, with the characteristic square-root collapse rate $O(\sqrt{T-t})$.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Yang

item.title: Quadratic Hubbard trees, automata, and ray connections
item.description: arXiv:2611.04190v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe an algorithm that, given a postcritically finite quadratic polynomial, outputs a finite state machine whose regular language is the set of angles whose dynamical rays land on the Hubbard tree, generalizing an example of Milnor. We do this by extracting orbit portraits from angled internal addresses, and constructing a suitable Markov partition of angle intervals. A main application is computing direct ray connections between Hubbard trees in matings of quadratic polynomials, and understanding when ray connections between the trees first appear when moving along veins of the Mandelbrot set. If one of the mating parameters is fixed, we prove that first ray connections are picked up at parabolic parameters or tips of veins. We also prove that the locus of parameter pairs in two given veins for which there are no ray connections between the trees is open. Additionally, we show that there are no ray connections between small Julia sets in matings of locally connected rabbit tunings.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Ventilari Sodr\'e

item.title: From elementary processes to chaos: a discrete-time two-stage contagion model and its continuous limit
item.description: arXiv:2611.08353v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two-stage contagion, in which adoption requires two contacts with adopters, combined with population turnover produces bistability and relaxation oscillations, but no chaos, in Katriel's differential equations. From the elementary reactions, without reference to the differential equations, we derive a discrete-time model in which the population is updated in rounds of length $\tau$, as in elections, meetings or turns of a game: each individual makes at most one transition per round, events compete as exponential risks, and adoptions take effect from the next round. The model is a Markov chain whose large-population limit is a map $F_\tau$; Katriel's equations are recovered as $\tau\to0$. Taking the probability $p$ of adoption after a single contact as bifurcation parameter, with rates and round length fixed, $F_\tau$ goes from extinction through a window of chaos to a stable equilibrium; for $\beta/\gamma=46$, $\mu/\gamma=0.002$, $\gamma\tau=5.5$ the computed window is $0.023\le p\le0.056$, bounded by the invasion threshold and by a boundary crisis beyond a subcritical Neimark--Sacker point. One-stage contagion ($p=1$), $p=0$ and permanent adoption showed no chaos in our scans. In all tests the chaotic attractor was unique up to coexistence with simpler attractors, with one positive Lyapunov exponent. In the same window Katriel's equations have a periodic relaxation cycle with troughs of $10^{-44}$--$10^{-164}$: the round structure does not create the oscillation but turns it into chaos and shrinks the oscillatory range in $p$ from $(0.022,0.41)$ to $(0.022,0.056)$. The chaos is thus not an artefact of discretising a stable state, but a property of two-stage contagion with synchronous updating.
item.dc:creator: Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no, Luca Meacci

item.title: h-dichotomies via uniform noncriticality and expansiveness for noninvertible evolution families
item.description: arXiv:2611.08451v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish characterizations of h-dichotomies for noninvertible evolution families acting on Banach spaces, in terms of appropriate notions of expansiveness and uniform noncriticality. Our results extend the corresponding characterizations previously obtained for invertible evolution families. To the best of our knowledge, no such characterizations have previously been established for general noninvertible evolution families. A key difference is that noninvertibility makes the structure of the stable spaces more delicate: in our positive-half-line result, finite codimension must be imposed at every time, rather than only at the initial time. We show by an example that the latter, weaker condition is insufficient. We also study evolution families on the negative half-line, using duality to obtain corresponding characterizations in terms of dual expansiveness and dual uniform noncriticality. General growth rates are treated by a time-rescaling argument.
item.dc:creator: Davor Dragicevic

item.title: Foliated and compactly supported isotopies of tubular neighborhoods
item.description: arXiv:2208.05876v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a foliation with a "singular" submanifold $\Sigma$ on a smooth manifold $A$ and $p:E \to \Sigma$ be a tubular neighborhood of $\Sigma$ in $A$. Under certain "scalability" assumptions on $\mathcal{F}$ near $\Sigma$, we prove that every leaf preserving diffeomorphism $h$ of $A$ is isotopic via a leaf preserving isotopy to a diffeomorphism which coincides with some vector bundle morphism of $E$ near $\Sigma$. This result is simultaneously a foliated, compactly supported and parametrized variant of a well known statement that every diffeomorphism $h$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ fixing the origin is isotopic to the linear isomorphism induced by its Jacobi matrix at $0$. Particular cases of such a "linearization theorem" allowed recently to compute homotopy types of leaf preserving diffeomorphism groups of polar Morse-Bott foliations on lens spaces and the twisted bundle $S^2\tilde{\times}S^1$. In general, that "linearization theorem" can be used to reduce the study of the homotopy type of the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $\mathcal{F}$ to an investigation of the following three groups (being independent in a certain sense): (a) diffeomorphism group of $\Sigma$, (b) the group of leaf preserving vector bundle isomorphisms of $E$, and (c) the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $A$ supported in $A\setminus \Sigma$, i.e. out of the "singularity" $\Sigma$.
item.dc:creator: Oleksandra Khokhliuk, Sergiy Maksymenko

item.title: On $q$-real and $q$-complex numbers
item.description: arXiv:2508.08440v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In arXiv:1812.00170 and arXiv:1908.04365, Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko introduced $q$-rational numbers $[x]_q$, rational functions specializing to $x$ at $q=1$, and their extension to $q$-real numbers, Laurent series agreeing with $[x]_q$ for rational $x$. It was conjectured in arXiv:2102.00891 that for every real $x>1$, $[x]_q$ has positive radius of convergence, with optimal common radius $R_*=(3-\sqrt{5})/2$, attained at the golden ratio. We prove that $[x]_q$ converges to a nonvanishing holomorphic function for every real $x>1$ and $|q|<3-2\sqrt{2}$. The proof gives an expansion of $1/[x]_q$ as a $q$-adically convergent series of rational functions, converging absolutely and locally uniformly on an explicit region. It also defines a positive analytic function for $q\in(-R_*,1)$. Using arXiv:2405.15970, we further obtain convergence for $|q|<2-\sqrt{3}$. We compute $[x]_q$ explicitly for some transcendental $x$, including ${\rm cotan}(1)$ and $e$. We also establish sharp inequalities for numerators and denominators of $q$-rationals when $|q|=1$ and determine the closure of the set of $[x]_q$ when such $q$ is not a root of unity. Next, we show that coefficientwise reduction modulo every $m\ge2$ is injective on the Cantor line (the extended real line with doubled up rationals and the Cantor set topology); for $m=2$, it identifies the Cantor line with $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_2((q)))$. We describe the inverse map, extend rationality results modulo every prime, characterize quadratic series over $\mathbb F_2(q)$ corresponding to quadratic irrationals, derive criteria for eventual parity of coefficients, and compute the real numbers corresponding to $1+q^n$. Finally, we propose a definition of $q$-complex number $[\tau]_q$, a meromorphic function in $\tau\in\mathbb C_+$ expressed via hypergeometric functions evaluated at modular functions of $\tau$.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Etingof

item.title: Generic classification of the quasi-free flows on the Cuntz algebra $\mathcal{O}_2$
item.description: arXiv:2509.00829v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article we show that the quasi-free flows on the Cuntz algebra $\mathcal{O}_2$ are generically classifiable by the inverse temperature of their unique KMS state. Along the way, we show that a large class of quasi-free flows on the Cuntz algebra $\mathcal{O}_n$ are generically equivariantly $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and their corresponding dual action has the Rokhlin property generically.
item.dc:creator: Robert Neagu

item.title: Convergence of optimizers implies eigenvalues filtering at equilibrium
item.description: arXiv:2510.09034v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ample empirical evidence in deep neural network training suggests that a variety of optimizers tend to find nearly global optima. In this article, we adopt the reversed perspective that convergence to an arbitrary point is assumed rather than proven, focusing on the consequences of this assumption. From this viewpoint, in line with recent advances on the edge-of-stability phenomenon, we argue that different optimizers effectively act as eigenvalue filters determined by their hyperparameters. Specifically, the standard gradient descent method inherently avoids the sharpest minima, whereas Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) algorithms go even further by actively favoring wider basins. Inspired by these insights, we propose two novel algorithms that exhibit enhanced eigenvalue filtering, effectively promoting wider minima. Our theoretical analysis leverages a generalized Hadamard--Perron stable manifold theorem and applies to general semialgebraic $C^2$ functions, without requiring additional non-degeneracy conditions or global Lipschitz bound assumptions. We support our conclusions with numerical experiments on feed-forward neural networks.

item.title: Global Analytical Solution of the Identical Kuramoto Model for N=3 via Koopman Eigenfunctions
item.description: arXiv:2605.07360v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Kuramoto model is a paradigmatic model of collective synchronization in coupled oscillator systems. Although its mathematical properties have been extensively investigated, explicit phase trajectories from arbitrary initial conditions have been available only for the simplest case, N = 2. In this study, we provide a global analytical solution for the phase trajectories of the all-to-all coupled Kuramoto model with three identical oscillators (N = 3). We construct Koopman eigenfunctions from products of observables whose growth rates, weighted by the exponents, sum to a constant, and obtain a nontrivial constant of motion from the ratio of two such eigenfunctions. Using their explicit exponential time dependence, we reduce trajectory reconstruction to time-dependent quartic equations and recover the phase trajectories. The same construction also yields Koopman eigenfunctions for the Kuramoto-Sakaguchi model with arbitrary phase lag and for the N = 4 all-to-all and ring-coupled systems. These results provide a concrete example in which Koopman eigenfunctions are used not only to characterize but also to explicitly solve a widely studied nonlinear model.
item.dc:creator: Keisuke Taga

item.title: Attention as In-Context Empirical Bayes: A Two-Stage View via Particle Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2605.29351v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study minimal attention-only transformers under all-token corruption and show they admit a two-stage empirical Bayes interpretation. A single attention step computes a kernel-weighted posterior mean with respect to the empirical distribution defined by the context. Depth refines this distribution through particle dynamics (Stage 1), while a long-range skip-connection carries the noisy input as a query for posterior inference (Stage 2), revealing distinct statistical roles for depth and attention residuals. The framework isolates a minimal setting in which the context itself induces a depth-dependent energy landscape governing in-context inference. We show that effective denoising can emerge without an explicit noise schedule: a fixed kernel bandwidth and finite integration horizon suffice, yielding a principled depth-noise relationship. We further establish a posterior-mean recovery guarantee for Gaussian priors, showing the empirical estimator converges to the Bayes-optimal predictor under sequential asymptotic conditions. Connecting these dynamics to reverse-diffusion limits, our results provide a statistical interpretation of attention as in-context inference via sample-based posterior estimation, without explicit density modeling.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Smart, Soumya Ganguly, Nilava Metya, Alexandre V. Morozov, Anirvan M. Sengupta

item.title: A criterion for weighted uniform distribution along functions from a Hardy field
item.description: arXiv:2606.08040v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A classical theorem of Boshernitzan states that if $f$ is a function which belongs to a Hardy field and which satisfies $|f(x)|\prec x^{\ell}$ for some $\ell\in \mathbb{N}$, then the sequence $(f(n))_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ is uniformly distributed modulo 1 if and only if $\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{|f(x)-p(x)|}{\log(x)} = \infty$ for all $p(x)\in \mathbb{Q}[x]$. We provide a new proof of this result using methods from summability theory and we extend Boshernitzan's criterion by obtaining necessary and sufficient conditions for $f$ to be uniformly distributed modulo 1 with respect to a broad class of weighted averages. As an application of our results, we show that for the function $f(x) = x^{3/2}$ and for any $(a,b)\subset [0,1]$, and all sufficiently large $N\in\mathbb{N}$, there is an $n\in [N-N^{\frac{1}{4}},N]$ such that $f(n)\mod 1\in (a,b)$.
item.dc:creator: Michael Reilly

item.title: Uniform $L^{\infty}$-Boundedness and Upper Semicontinuity of Global Attractors for Reaction--Diffusion Equations with Neumann Boundary Conditions on Uniform Jones Domains
item.description: arXiv:2607.08061v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider a family of semilinear parabolic equations with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions on a family of varying non-smooth domains $\{\Omega_\mu\}_{\mu \in \Lambda} \subset \mathbb{R}^n $. Assuming only that the domains have uniformly bounded volumes, bounded away from zero, and satisfy a uniform Jones condition, together with the usual structural requirements on the linear and nonlinear terms, we establish the well-posedness of the problem in an appropriate scale of fractional Banach spaces and prove the existence of global attractors. The attractors themselves are shown to be uniformly bounded in $L^{\infty}(\Omega_\mu)$ by an elementary truncation argument, which uses no property of the domains beyond the weak formulation of the Neumann condition. A Moser--Alikakos bootstrap iteration, in conjunction with the uniform Gronwall lemma and the uniform properties of the Jones extension operator, then yields the stronger statement that bounded sets of $L^{q}(\Omega_\mu)$ are absorbed, in finite time and uniformly in $\mu$, into a fixed ball of $L^{\infty}(\Omega_\mu)$; this iteration uses only first-order Sobolev embeddings, which is what makes it available on domains where the domain of the elliptic operator is not contained in $H^{2}$. Finally, assuming the volume convergence of the domains, $|\Omega_\mu \triangle \Omega_0| \to 0$, we construct a framework of connecting maps, show that the uniform Jones condition upgrades this convergence in measure to Mosco convergence of the associated bilinear forms, and prove that the family of attractors is upper semicontinuous at $\mu = 0$ in $L^2(\Omega_\mu)$ and hence, by interpolation, in $H^s(\Omega_\mu)$ for every $s<1$.

item.title: Uniform Exponential Stability Analysis of Impulsive Linear Time-Invariant Systems on Banach and Hilbert Spaces: Non-Coercive and Coercive Stability Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2607.17260v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the uniform exponential stability analysis of infinite-dimensional impulsive systems defined on a Banach or Hilbert space, whose flow is governed by a fixed $C_0$-semigroup generator and whose jumps occur at a prescribed time sequence. While the flow and jump maps are themselves time-invariant, the time-triggered impulses render the propagator a genuinely time-varying evolution family, which is the source of the analysis difficulty addressed here. We combine ideas from hybrid systems theory and infinite-dimensional systems to produce operator-based stability conditions, which can be analytically or numerically checked via convex programming. Necessary and sufficient conditions for the uniform exponential stability of impulsive systems on Banach spaces are obtained in the context of a fixed impulse-times sequence but also of arbitrary, constant, minimum, and range dwell-times using both non-coercive and coercive Lyapunov functionals. Some of those results are then adapted to systems on a Hilbert space and quadratic Lyapunov functionals. As an application, linear switched systems are shown to be an exact special case: reformulated as impulsive systems with unit-norm selector jumps, they inherit non-coercive and clock-dependent dwell-time stability conditions on both Banach and Hilbert spaces. Theoretical and numerical examples are given for illustration, notably on the sampled-data control of time-delay systems.
item.dc:creator: Corentin Briat, Francesco Ferrante, Christophe Prieur

item.title: Increased-order generalized synchronization in memristive neurons: dissipativity analysis and data-driven control
item.description: arXiv:2610.25164v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate increased-order generalized synchronization between four- and five-dimensional memristive Hindmarsh--Rose neurons, focusing on the selection and stabilization of the synchronization map. An analytical construction combines a prescribed nonlinear map with adaptive control, retaining the memristive switching contribution explicitly in the error dynamics. Lyapunov analysis establishes asymptotic synchronization under uniform strict dissipativity and yields a switching-independent decrease estimate outside an explicit error neighborhood. Numerical simulations exhibit error decay beyond the sufficient convergence conditions. A complementary data-driven construction uses next-generation reservoir computing to learn predictors from uncoupled full-state trajectories and an affine synchronization map through dynamical consistency. The resulting sampled-data controller achieves small residual tracking errors without access to the governing equations. Relative to a reference map within the data-driven framework, the learned map reduces median control effort approximately eightfold while improving tracking accuracy. These results connect synchronization-map selection with conditional convergence guarantees and reduced control requirements.
item.dc:creator: Dennis Mustafi\'{c}, Marius E. Yamakou

item.title: Amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations and applications to anti-treeability
item.description: arXiv:2610.32038v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the structure of amenable subrelations of treeable measure-class-preserving equivalence relations, applying the Radon--Nikodym topography perspective initiated in our companion paper [TTD25]. For a nowhere smooth amenable subrelation, we show that the ends selected by each class in Adams's end selection theorem are precisely those which are nonvanishing along that class. From this, we derive a number of structure results about nowhere smooth amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations. For example, we show that every nowhere smooth amenable subrelation is contained in an essentially unique maximal amenable subrelation. This yields an anti-treeability criterion, which we use to show that every nonamenable locally compact second countable group with noncompact amenable radical is not treeable, and that every nonamenable nonunimodular treeable group has a compact open subgroup.
item.dc:creator: Anush Tserunyan, Robin Tucker-Drob

item.title: Automaticity of structural defects in fixed points of block substitutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.04880v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study structural defects in fixed points of block substitutions, building on arXiv:2604.12637 and providing its technical supplement. We develop an automata-based framework to characterize their occurrence and derive verifiable combinatorial criteria. We also introduce simplifications for the construction and analysis of these automata, including tensor-product decompositions, that clarify the mechanisms underlying structural defects and their emergence.
item.dc:creator: Lior Tenenbaum

item.title: Geometric folding and maximal asymptotic variance
item.description: arXiv:2611.09697v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Based on the recent breakthroughs by OpenAI and consequently by Binder-Ivrii-Prause-Smirnov, we develop a finite-scale folding method for the nonlinearity of a schlicht function, based on a signed critical-point count for superharmonic potentials and a quantitative target cutoff. Furthermore, we use a cylindrical root transform to reduce the logarithmic cost of access to the point at infinity. Combined with a Littlewood-Paley formula as well as dilation, the method yields the maximal asymptotic variance bound $\Sigma_{\max}^2\le1$ for the unrestricted schlicht class of normalized univalent functions.
